mcqs.question: A solid cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm is melted and recast into a cube. What is the side length of the cube?
mcqs.explanation: When a solid is recast, its volume remains the same. Volume of the cylinder = πr²h = π·3²·5 = 45π cm³. Let the side of the cube be s; then s³ = 45π, so s = (45π)^{1/3} ≈ 5.2 cm. Options that use surface‑area equality (e.g., 7.5 cm) are incorrect because volume, not surface area, is conserved.

mcqs.question: A solid sphere of radius r cm is melted and recast into a right circular cone whose base radius is 6 cm and height is 12 cm. Find the value of r (correct to two decimal places).
mcqs.explanation: Volume is conserved. Volume of cone = (1/3)π·6²·12 = 144π cm³. Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³. Equate: (4/3)πr³ = 144π ⇒ r³ = 108 ⇒ r = 108^{1/3} ≈ 4.76 cm. The other options arise from incorrect algebra or ignoring the factor 4/3.

mcqs.question: A metal block has a volume of 0.02 m³. It is melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the radius of the sphere in centimeters?
mcqs.explanation: First convert the volume to cm³: 0.02 m³ = 0.02 × (100 cm)³ = 0.02 × 1,000,000 cm³ = 20,000 cm³. For a sphere, (4/3)πr³ = 20,000 ⇒ r³ = 20,000·3/(4π) = 15,000/π ≈ 4,774 ⇒ r ≈ 10.5 cm. Options that ignore unit conversion give much smaller radii.

mcqs.question: A cylindrical wooden log 1 m long has a radius of 10 cm. It is melted and recast into a solid sphere. Which statement is true?

options.A: The radius of the sphere will be greater than 10 cm.
options.B: The radius of the sphere will be less than 10 cm.
options.C: The radius of the sphere will be exactly 10 cm.
options.D: The sphere will have the same surface area as the cylinder.

mcqs.answer: The radius of the sphere will be greater than 10 cm.
mcqs.explanation: Volume of cylinder = πr²h = π·10²·100 = 10,000π cm³ (since 1 m = 100 cm). For a sphere, (4/3)πR³ = 10,000π ⇒ R³ = 7,500 ⇒ R ≈ 19.7 cm, which is greater than 10 cm. Surface area is not conserved, so option D is false, and options B and C contradict the calculated radius.
